question: Which of the following antibiotics could be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has hypersensitivity to penicillin" -> "Avoidance of penicillin and related beta-lactams" -> "Piperacillin/tazobactam is a penicillin derivative" -> "Not suitable for this patient" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Patient has hypersensitivity to penicillin" -> "Aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic" -> "Monobactams are generally safe for penicillin-allergic patients" -> "Aztreonam can be used" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Patient has hypersensitivity to penicillin" -> "Ampicillin is a penicillin derivative" -> "Not suitable for this patient" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Patient has hypersensitivity to penicillin" -> "Amoxicillin is a penicillin derivative" -> "Not suitable for this patient" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has hypersensitivity to penicillin" -> "Ceftazidime is a cephalosporin antibiotic" -> "Some cephalosporins may cross-react with penicillin" -> "Ceftazidime may be used with caution" -> 70%
analysis: Aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic that is generally considered safe for patients with a history of penicillin allergy, as it has a different side chain structure and does not cross-react with penicillin. The other options, including piperacillin/tazobactam, ampicillin, amoxicillin, and ceftazidime, are either penicillin derivatives or have a higher likelihood of cross-reactivity due to their beta-lactam structure.
